correctness.rationale: In u=(ωq,p), midpoint acts via orthogonal Cayley matrix R(t), t=ωH/2, with complex second harmonic Z=((1+it)/(1−it))². Independence multiplies E(z_k²) by conjugate E(Z)^k and preserves tr S, proving iff for universal isotropy and all future steps. Rational Re/Im formulas yield exact identity t−(1−ReZ−ImZ)/2 = t(t−1)²(t²+2t+3)/(1+t²)² >=0. Integrating against any nonnegative H of finite mean with EZ=0 gives E t>=1/2. Equality support only t=0,1, with unique equal masses since Z(0)=1,Z(1)=−1. For every m=ωμ>1, s=(m+2−sqrt(m²+8))/2 in (0,1), r=(1+s)/(1−s), s+r=m and Z(s)=−Z(r), making the two positive H values isotropize at mean μ. Arc Z([0,T]) subtends angle <π iff T<1, separating zero from convex hull; at T=1 exact endpoint law requires H=0, and T>1 enables strictly positive pair. I rederived exact symbolic polynomial identity and quarter-turn parameters, separately from packaged checker. Applicability only to second moments with independent initial law, not full phase uniformization.

final_claim: For a fixed-frequency harmonic oscillator under iid independent nonnegative random-time implicit midpoint, universal one-step isotropization of uncentered second moments iff E[((1+iωH/2)/(1−iωH/2))^2]=0; all such laws E H>=1/ω with unique minimizing law H=0 or 2/ω each probability 1/2; every larger mean admits strictly positive equiprobable two-point law and bounded timesteps are feasible exactly when cap>=2/ω (strict-positive cap>2/ω).
limitations: Fixed ω>0 planar linear harmonic oscillator only; iid required for k>1, independent exogenous H for one-step.
Uncentered moments, centered covariance only initially centered ensemble; isotropization not angular uniformity or trajectory accuracy.
